sentences.text:
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2.

The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.161 of 2024, under Sections 323, 504, 506,
354, 376 IPC, Police Station Bilgram, District Hardoi.
3. In terms of the FIR lodged under Section 354 IPC, it was alleged that the applicant, who was related as a brother to the victim, use to touch her inappropriately.
It was also stated that he touch her inappropriately on various occasions.

In the statement under Section 161 of Cr.P.C., the victim disclosed her age as 25 years and also stated that the applicant was the brother of the informant and Pankaj Kumar vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home, ... on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168739467/
1 used to come home regularly and used to touch her inappropriately.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As he was a member of the family, she never raised any alarm and subsequently, as he was threatened, an FIR in question was lodged.
The medical of the victim was done on 22.03.2024 did not corroborate any allegation of any injury.
The internal examination was not done as there was no allegation of offence of rape.
The radiological age of the victim was assessed as 19 years.

The victim stated that around one year ago,
on the false pretext of marriage, physical relations were formed in between them on various occasions.
It was also stated that some inappropriate video was made and based upon which, the applicant used to blackmail her.
4. Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail prayer.

5. Considering the huge variance in the allegations contained in the FIR and the statements under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C. coupled with the fact that the victim herself disclosed her age as 25 years and as per the medical examination, her age is 19 years and the fact the applicant has no criminal antecedents and is languishing in jail since 21.05.2024, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

6. Let the applicant Pankaj Kumar be released on bail in the abovesaid first information report number on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
